title: Window
detail: Entries 6:30-8:30 PT only. Everything is closed by 8:56.
evidence: Your trades after 9:00 lost -$347; the model has none.

title: Trigger: EMA 8 turn
detail: Signal only on the 1-min bar where the EMA 8 turns your way after 3 bars pointing against. Order goes in at the first quote after that bar closes, paying the ask.
evidence: 93% of model buys happen the bar the EMA 8 turns. 84% have the last candle closed their way.

title: Setup 1: TRAP (reversal after a flush)
detail: Calls: yesterday's daily candle green AND QQQ at least $1.00 below yesterday's low. Puts: yesterday red AND QQQ $1.00+ above yesterday's high. Every EMA 8 turn inside the zone can fire.

title: Setup 2: GAP-AND-GO
detail: Opening gap of $2.50+ in the trade direction, nearest GEX strike at least $1.00 away, and last week's candle in the same direction. Max 2 per day, 30 min apart.

title: Conflicts
detail: Max 2 positions open. If a trap is active on one side, a gap-and-go on the other side is blocked. 10 minutes between signals on the same side.

title: Option choice
detail: The option nearest the money inside the price band, IV at or under 35%. Typical buy: 0.40 delta, about $1 out of the money, about 1.15.
evidence: Your typical buy: 0.26 delta, $3 out of the money.

title: Size
detail: 7 contracts when the spot is clear: at least 0.50 from the nearest level and 0.75 of room to the next one. Otherwise 3.

title: Stop
detail: -0.85 on the option from the mid at entry (about 2 QQQ of room at 0.40 delta).
evidence: Your stop: median 0.15, about 0.58 QQQ at your 0.26 delta.

title: Lock
detail: Once the option is +0.30, the stop moves to -0.15.

title: Take profit
detail: Once +0.50 has been reached, sell at the bid of the first quote after the EMA 8 ticks against you.

title: Time stop
detail: 90 minutes or 8:56, whichever comes first.

title: EMA 8 carry
detail: The EMA 8 is carried over from yesterday's last bar, so the first turns of the day are real.

title: Calls
detail: Calls carry the model.

title: With the morning trend
detail: Trades that end up with the 6:30-9:00 move.

title: Last week down
detail: Mostly trap calls after a down week.

title: 0.50-1.00 from a level
detail: Same sweet spot as yours.

title: Trend days
detail: It goes with the trend 17 of 20 times.

title: Puts
detail: Thin: few trades and a small average.

title: Against the morning trend
detail: Still positive, but small.

title: Wednesday and Friday
detail: Lower average, not negative.

title: Stops
detail: A full stop costs about -$37 per contract.

title: Days it sits out
detail: No trap and no gap-and-go: no trade.
evidence: Sat out 39 of 66 mornings (16 trend, 14 chop, 9 mixed).

title: What you are
detail: A counter-trend reversal scalper: you fade the move and try to buy the turn.
evidence: Median buy: QQQ 0.64 against you over 15 min, $1.00 on the wrong side of VWAP.

title: Your edge
detail: Small pullbacks, 0.50-1.00 from a level, pressing the same side after a win, fading a clean move.
evidence: Small pullback +$392; 0.50-1.00 from a level +$234; same side after a win +$464 (69% win).

title: What breaks it
detail: Buying while the push is still going, a scalper's stop on a reversal trade, trend days, tangled EMAs, tilt after a loss.
evidence: Hard push -$315; on a level -$345; trend days -$450; tangled EMAs -$550; after a loss 106 trades -$824.

title: One line
detail: A reversal trader's read with a scalper's risk habits. Wait for the turn to show, give it room, sit out days with no clean move.

title: Is there a model setup today?
detail: No trap and no gap-and-go means no trade.
evidence: No-setup days: 97 of your trades, -$148; a wide stop there made it worse (-$421).

title: Am I on the model's side?
detail: Never trade against an active setup.
evidence: Against the model: -$113; Oct 20 you bought puts while the model's call made +$526 per contract.

title: Did QQQ just push hard against me?
detail: More than 0.50 in 3 min: wait for it to stop.
evidence: Hard push: 42 trades, -$315, 14% win; QQQ kept going 0.69 against.

title: Has one candle closed my way?
detail: Wait for the first candle out of the dip.
evidence: Candle your way +$83; doji -$486. Model: 84% of buys.

title: Am I sitting on a level?
detail: Under 0.50 from a level: wait for the break or the reject.

title: Delta 0.35-0.50, IV under 35%?
detail: Buy near the money, skip high IV.
evidence: Your 0.25-0.50 delta trades lost -$335 with a 0.15 stop; model buys 0.40 delta.

title: Stop wide enough?
detail: -0.85 on the option, lock at +0.30, sell on the EMA 8 tick after +0.50.
evidence: Same entries on the model's side: -$153 became +$974.

title: Two losses in a row?
detail: Done for the day.

title: Before 8:30?
detail: No new trades after 8:30, none after 9:00.

title: Alerts not built yet
detail: The model only helps live if one engine sends one call and never flips sides mid-trade.

title: Dashboard clock bug at the DST change
detail: The GEX dashboard hard-codes the open as 13:30 UTC. Daylight saving ends Sun Nov 1, so from Mon Nov 2 the open is 14:30 UTC and the clock is an hour off.

title: Sample size
detail: 66 mornings, 58 model trades. The best day (Oct 20) is 22% of the total.

title: Puts are thin
detail: Only 15 put trades, +$8.50 per contract average.
evidence: Watch puts live before trusting them at size.

title: High-IV days untested
detail: The IV cap skips anything over 35%. Those setups are logged, not traded.

title: Bar source
detail: Live bars are IEX; the backtest used the full tape. Minor differences in turn timing are possible.

title: Human execution
detail: The replay assumes every signal is taken, the stop is left alone, and no extra trades are added.
evidence: Your history: tightening stops, re-buying, trading after 9:00.

title: 1 contract per signal
detail: Run the model exactly as built (up to 2 open, trap wins), 1 contract each. Never the 7/3 sizing at this account size.
evidence: Worst 2-week drop $130 at 1 contract. A 7-lot costs up to ~$1,080 and one stop is ~-$650.

title: 2-week breaker at -$120
detail: Down $120 in the current 2-week period: no new trades until the next period.
evidence: Replay: 1.8% of random 2-week stretches lose more than $120. Pessimistic case: 11%.

title: One stop is most of the budget
detail: A full stop at 1 contract costs $85-112 with slippage and fees. After one stop, the next trade is the last one for the period.

title: Account size changes the percentage, not the dollars
detail: $600 or $1,000: the same $130 worst drawdown, 22% vs 13%. Both can still buy a contract after it.
evidence: Option cost per contract: median $118, max $154.

title: Size up only from profit
detail: Add a 2nd contract only once profit covers two full stops (about $200), so a double stop comes out of winnings, not income. The exact threshold is your call.
evidence: Up to 2 positions can be open at once, so two stops in one morning is possible (3 days had 2 losses).

title: Up to 2 open beats 1 at a time
detail: At 1 contract, allowing 2 open positions was safer and earned more than 1 at a time.

title: 1. Yesterday's candle
detail: Green: only trap CALLS are possible today. Red: only trap PUTS.
evidence: Trap needs yesterday's candle on the trade's side.

title: 2. The trap line
detail: Calls: yesterday's low minus $1.00. Puts: yesterday's high plus $1.00. Write it down before 6:30. No touch, no trap.
evidence: Trap zone reached by 8:30 on 21 of 66 mornings.

title: 3. Last week's candle + the gap
detail: Gap-and-go calls need a gap up of $2.50+ and last week up. Puts need a gap down of $2.50+ and last week down. The nearest GEX level must be $1+ away.

title: 4. News at 5:30 PT?
detail: CPI mornings have been the model's weak spot. Consider half size or sitting out until more data says otherwise.
evidence: CPI mornings: 9 trades, -$110 at 1 contract, 44% winners.

title: 5. Nothing armed?
detail: No trap line and no gap-and-go means no trade today. That was 39 of 66 mornings.

title: CPI mornings
detail: The one release that hurt: 4 CPI mornings in the data.
evidence: 9 trades, -$110 at 1 contract (-$66 at 7/3), 44% winners. No-release mornings: 44 trades, +$16,137.

title: CPI mornings
detail: Small sample (4 mornings), but the only negative release type.
evidence: Watch the next CPI (Tue Nov 10) before trading it at size.

title: Not luck: timing
detail: Random entry times on the same days and sides, same exits: median +$1,389 vs the model +$2,815. 1 of 300 random runs beat it.
evidence: The EMA 8 turn timing roughly doubles what the day-and-side filter alone gets.

title: Not luck: side
detail: Random side and time on the same days: median +$201. None of 300 beat the model.
evidence: Picking the side (trap/gap rules) is most of the edge.

title: Walk-forward
detail: Settings picked only on earlier months made money in the next month, and all 60 setting combinations tested were positive in both test months.

title: IV cap
detail: Removing the 35% IV cap adds 11 trades worth +$75 at 1 contract. The cap costs almost nothing and avoids the wildest days.
